{{No footnotes|date=July 2024}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Ruziewicz problem''' (sometimes '''Banach–Ruziewicz problem''') in [[measure theory]] asks whether the usual [[Lebesgue measure]] on the [[N-sphere|''n''-sphere]] is characterised, up to proportionality, by its properties of being [[finitely additive]], invariant under [[rotation]]s, and defined on all [[Lebesgue measurable]] sets. 

This was answered affirmatively and independently for ''n'' ≥ 4 by [[Grigory Margulis]] and [[Dennis Sullivan]] around 1980, and for ''n'' = 2 and 3 by [[Vladimir Drinfeld]] (published 1984). It fails for the [[circle]].

The problem is named after [[Stanisław Ruziewicz]].
